paper_title: An analysis of vaccine-related sentiments from development to deployment   of COVID-19 vaccines
caption: : Caption not extracted
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how the number of observations (“Counts”) varies across sentiment “Polarity scores,” shown as a single connected line with point markers. The x-axis is labeled “Polarity scores,” uses a linear scale, and spans roughly from −1.1 on the left to 0.6 on the right, with regularly spaced tick labels at about 0.2-unit intervals (−1.0, −0.8, −0.6, −0.4, −0.2, 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6). The y-axis is labeled “Counts,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0 up to 50,000, with major ticks at 10,000-count intervals. A single blue solid line with circular markers starts near zero counts at the most negative polarity values (around −1.1 to −0.8), rises to several thousand by around −0.6 to −0.5 (approximately 1,000 to 4,500), then increases through the negative-to-neutral region (about 5,500 near −0.3 and ~11,000 near −0.2) to a prominent peak at approximately 0.0 polarity close to 49,000 counts; after this peak it drops to roughly 18,000 around 0.1, rises again to about 27,000 around 0.2, falls to about 8,500 around 0.3, dips to near 0 around 0.4, shows a smaller spike near 0.5 at roughly 9,500, and ends near 0 again around 0.55–0.6.
